mathematical_steps: The two specified generators belong to the fiber product defined by phi(g)=c^j. Projection of this full fiber product has exactly the cyclic kernel generated by(1,u^p).
The marked subgroup projects onto G0 because a0,b0 generate it. Its element b^(2p)=(1,u^(-2p)) generates the complete kernel because p is odd, so the marked subgroup equals the full fiber product.

Orders in the direct product give p^2,2p^2 and2. The cyclic subgroup generated by a projects injectively; any element shared with the subgroup generated by b therefore vanishes because the base cyclic intersection is trivial.

A hypothetical simultaneous inversion preserves the kernel generated by b^(2p), induces an automorphism of the quotient, and would invert both base generators. This contradicts the stated NoReverser premise.

The standard rotation-group/polyhedron correspondence remains a retained geometric input. Neither characteristicity under arbitrary automorphisms nor preservation of chirality by arbitrary covers is assumed.
